# Tagcast 1.7.0

Tagcast 1.7.0 combines the completed browsing, visualization and lyrics work with
the stabilization fixes from the independent repository audits. The desktop app
and Python/browser interface continue to share the same editor, player and data
safeguards. Tagcast never retags your existing local music files.

## Browsing and discovery

- Optional continuous browsing extends artist, album, category and favourite
  shelves across pages while keeping the document's normal scrolling. Returning
  from an album restores the browsing position, filters and ordering.
- Random Order reshuffles the complete album shelf independently of starting
  playback. Search and filtering continue to work with the selected order.
- Ordinary categories, favourites, playlists and tags reuse an already loaded,
  account-bound library snapshot instead of repeatedly requesting upstream status.
  Browsing can continue through a temporary upstream outage when a valid snapshot
  is available. Explicit refresh still refreshes, and remote writes still check
  fresh state and perform their required read-back.

## Eight optional music visualizations

- Expanded Now playing offers Aurora, Orbit, Ribbons, LED, Scope, Radial, Stars
  and Waterfall, including locally bundled Butterchurn/MilkDrop effects.
- Random mode gives each effect a turn and rotates after 30 seconds of visible
  playback. Pausing, seeking, buffering or hiding the view does not advance the
  active-playback clock. Effects share the existing analyser and audio element.
- Effects respect reduced motion. Unsupported rendering or a visualization error
  falls back to artwork without stopping playback. No presets or visualizations
  are downloaded from an external service.

## Safer settings and reviewed writes

- Settings are validated as a complete submission before being applied. Invalid
  keys, partial validation failures and failed persistence leave the existing
  configuration, OAuth scopes and runtime service state consistent.
- Ambiguous mutation responses now start safe read-back verification where the
  operation can be identified. Confirmed success, failure and an unknown outcome
  remain distinct; remote mutations are never automatically retried.
- Playlist creation without a returned ID remains unknown. A matching name alone
  is never treated as proof that a specific creation succeeded.
- Album lyrics import review reuses reviewed snapshots without skipping fresh
  save guards, preservation of unrelated userdata or per-track verification.
  Import remains explicit, reviewed and serialized.

## Reliable shutdown and playback recovery

- Closing the desktop app keeps a visible finishing window while accepted writes,
  read-backs and required storage work settle. Idle connections, streams and
  interruptible work no longer keep the application invisibly alive.
- A second launch focuses the finishing window. Keep Tagcast open restores the
  same backend and drafts; it does not resend a mutation or resume stopped work.
  There is no blanket deadline that kills an accepted critical write.
- A recoverable temporary audio failure gets one bounded recovery attempt for the
  same queue entry and position. Pause, seek, track/account changes, mini-player
  controls and playback history remain synchronized. Authorization failures are
  not disguised by repeated reloads or silent quality downgrades.
- Experimental Gapless Playback remains optional and off by default. Unsupported
  transitions use ordinary playback. Universal sample accuracy across every
  format, device and platform is not claimed.

## Security, interface and maintenance

- The Python-served browser interface now sends a Content Security Policy derived
  from the same rules as Electron. Legitimate early inline scripts are authorized
  by SHA-256 hashes; JavaScript unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval are not enabled.
- HEAD requests enforce the existing Host validation; generated static directory
  listings are disabled. Invalid, negative, ambiguous and oversized body lengths
  are rejected before body processing or mutation admission.
- Visible status toasts remain accessible and readable while allowing pointer
  interaction with controls beneath them, including the narrow-screen theme menu.
- The directly imported requests library is now a direct dependency. Existing
  dependency versions were not broadly upgraded as part of that correction.
- Third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to verified immutable commits, with
  Dependabot proposals retained for separate review. Existing permissions and
  release/signing gates remain intact.
- The desktop runtime is Electron 44.11.0, within major 44, with upstream
  graphics/media maintenance and the preceding Linux and ASAR fixes. No major-45
  update or new Electron menu functionality is included.
- Collection test teardown now invalidates pending cache writers before removing
  temporary files and waits for active writes, fixing the reproduced Windows
  cleanup race without changing production cache or write semantics.

## Downloads, upgrading and signing

Downloads include macOS Apple Silicon and Intel ZIPs, a Windows x64 ZIP, a Linux
x64 TAR.GZ and a Debian/Ubuntu amd64 installer, each with a SHA-256 companion.
The release pipeline requires all native checks, Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 installation
validation and final distribution verification before publication. Production
macOS archives require Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, Apple notarization,
a valid stapled ticket and Gatekeeper acceptance after extraction; ad-hoc test
packages are not substituted for production downloads.

Quit the older app before upgrading. Existing settings, sign-in data and local
preferences are preserved. macOS requires 13 Ventura or newer; Linux requires a
graphical desktop and compatible libraries. Keep the complete extracted package
together and retain Chromium's sandbox. Python 3.11+ browser use and the bundled
tagcast-cli remain available. The illustrated PDF manual remains the labelled
1.4.0 edition; the Wiki documents newer functionality.

## Known limitations and accepted residual risks

- **Playlist append contract (F2-02):** the real service's exact behavior when a
  destination already contains intentional duplicate positions is still unverified.
  Current append verification and the mock assume whole-list deduplication. Passing
  mock tests do not establish duplicate-position preservation. No real-account
  write experiment was performed and append semantics were not changed speculatively.
  Where repeated positions matter, retain the original ordered list and inspect
  fresh library data after an append. An uncertain result
  must not be treated as a reason to repeat a potentially completed mutation.
- Physical Linux Wayland coverage remains incomplete. CI's Linux GUI checks use
  X11/Xvfb; window-manager-specific behaviour is not universally established.
- Windows Authenticode signing through SignPath remains deferred. Windows downloads
  are unsigned and can show SmartScreen warnings; obtain them from this official
  release and verify their checksums.
- Hardware audio compatibility cannot be exhaustively verified. Synthetic PCM
  measurements capture before physical output and are not an AirPlay, Bluetooth
  or hardware-output accuracy guarantee.
- Seven previously documented moderate npm build-dependency package findings
  remain outside this focused release. They were not silently resolved through an
  unrelated dependency overhaul.

These documented limitations were accepted for 1.7.0. Failed mandatory tests,
signing/notarization, archive integrity checks or evidence of data loss still
block publication; they are not covered by that acceptance.

[Code signing policy](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast#code-signing-policy)
and [privacy policy](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v1.7.0/PRIVACY.md).
